harbor_p17_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_001.text: The nineteenth week's fire began with a smell the warehouse keeper mistook for somebody's breakfast. The stove in the break corner had been lit for its permitted ordinary use, and the reported roof patch still awaited that afternoon's follow-up. A worker opened the shutter because the smell seemed unusually sharp. Then she saw a thin brown thread curling beneath the repaired section above the flue. She called the keeper rather than lifting a ceiling board herself. He rang the ordinary alarm and gave the spoken evacuation direction to the people nearest him. Smoke thickened before the first bucket arrived.

harbor_p17_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_002.text: Yue heard the alarm from the contact room, where she was halfway through a permitted reply. Han looked toward the doorway and then at the two waiting people. The office's evacuation plan did not yet require this inland room to close, but its keeper would assess the smoke route. Yue finished handing the current reply to its owner and received a clear task from the contact lead: take the confirmed receiving status to the shelter desk on foot by the dry inland lane. She left the official file with Han. Her own pack stayed in her checked lodging.

harbor_p17_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_003.text: At the warehouse, the supervisor called names against the ordinary attendance sheet while a second worker guided visitors through the clear exit. Five people came out from the occupied work area. The keeper counted six expected, including himself, then realized the rear sorter had not reached the doorway. He shouted her name and received no answer through the smoke. Yan's rigging crew had stopped its adjacent loading task at the alarm. The assigned fire crew was already approaching from the nearby station. Yan passed the missing person's last known position to its leader instead of sending Bo inside.

harbor_p17_004.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_p17_004.text: Put the last place on the site plan and tell the fire leader which entrance was open. We do not turn one missing person into two by guessing through smoke. Bo, take these workers beyond the receiving line and keep the load path clear. I know the buckets look like something anybody can carry, but the crew needs its own route first. You can help at the outside water line when its leader assigns you. Tell the supervisor who left and who is still unconfirmed. Speak the names. Do not say everybody is out because five faces look like enough.

harbor_p17_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_005.text: The sorter, a woman called Bao, reached the side door coughing before the interior search team crossed its threshold. She had moved away from the smoke toward a lower clear passage and found the latch stiff. The ordinary team opened it from outside after hearing her call. They received her immediately, closed the search status and directed the care attendant toward her. The warehouse keeper began thanking every person near him. Bao could not answer. Yue arrived at the sheltered receiving point with the office status and saw the attendant move everyone else back so she could breathe.

harbor_p17_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_006.text: Bao's distress frightened Yue more than the flame now visible at the roof edge. An injury could look small from a distance and fill a person's whole body when she stood near it. The attendant arranged the prescribed ordinary care and transport, using the established injury receiving process for the emergency interval. Yue took only the permitted household contact request after Bao could give it. Her cousin worked in an inland kitchen and needed a confirmed message, not a rumor of a woman lost in a warehouse. The runner received the exact name and location within his assigned route.

harbor_p17_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_007.text: The warehouse's ordinary water supply fed the crew line from its marked access, but the hand pump failed its first stroke. A worker reported the failure at once. The fire leader switched to the already identified public trough source and requested the rated hired pump available through the emergency equipment category. Yan organized the outside hauling line under the crew's direction. Bo carried empty buckets back without racing the full ones through them. The work looked simple until Yue watched three people nearly reach for the same handle. Then the leader set the rhythm aloud, and the confusion became motion.

harbor_p17_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_008.text: The replacement captain, covering Sui's approved leave, opened the authorized fire receiving plan with the harbor master. The remaining emergency categories had actual limits. A ten-copper ordinary pump hire came from equipment; five extra half-shifts at two copper made ten for the assigned receiving and clearance work. The technical keeper left the four unused fragment-screen stones locked. An anchored spray and fragment screen did not become a fire wall because people needed one. The fire crew used water, clearance, safe entry decisions and the building's ordinary boundaries. Nobody waited for the light they had seen during the storm.

harbor_p17_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_009.text: A merchant ran toward the main warehouse door shouting about his cloth. The keeper stopped him behind the receiving line and explained that the crew had evacuated everyone confirmed on site. The merchant said the cloth would ruin him. It might, and the fire leader still refused an unsafe retrieval. Yue knew the cloth trader by sight from the partnership's declined offer. His distress did not make that earlier disagreement satisfying. He was a person watching property burn, not a lesson about exclusivity. She asked which contact he wanted called. He gave his daughter's name after swearing at her once.

harbor_p17_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_010.text: The trader's daughter arrived with the aunt whose account shop employed Aning. They stood together beyond the barrier. The girl did not ask the crew to reenter. She asked her father whether the stock list existed elsewhere. He said it did, then accused himself of remembering a paper while the cloth burned. The aunt said the copy would help later and did not change what they were watching now. Yue carried that source status only to the receiving clerk. Aning stayed at work under the roster until her aunt sent the confirmed family message. Nobody summoned her through a guess.

harbor_p17_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_011.text: He Ming saw smoke from the partnership window and went to the doorway with Zhou. Their own stock had never entered the warehouse because the follow-up had been deferred. For one instant she felt relieved enough to smile. Then she saw the trader at the barrier and hated the smile she had not quite made. An Shou asked whether the fire might spread to their room. They consulted the actual street clearance direction rather than settle the question by watching the roof. The incident lead ordered the adjacent working strip evacuated, including their room, while the crew assessed the smoke.

harbor_p17_012.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p17_012.text: Leave the wrapping where it is. We are not going to carry a new stack through somebody's water line because it happens to be ours. We have the room's stock list in our private notebook, and the buyer's parcels are not here today. Zhou, bring the notebook if it is already beside you. An, lock only if the supervisor says the door should be shut; do not delay for it. We go to the receiving place and tell Wu the job is paused. She has children elsewhere and should hear the actual status before the smoke tells her something worse.

harbor_p17_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_013.text: Wu was at the canteen, where the windows faced away from the warehouse. A neighbor brought the closure message through the agreed contact route, and she asked immediately about the children's supervised room. It lay inland beyond the evacuation strip and its keeper had confirmed everyone there. Wu stayed for the current canteen handover, then went by the safe road. Her older child wanted to see the fire. She said no and made the explanation shorter than the child wanted. The duck, untroubled in its basket, supplied a hiss that seemed to support her authority more reliably than any neighbor.

harbor_p17_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_014.text: Han's office keeper closed the smoke-facing window and moved the public receiving table farther inside after the site report. The room itself remained usable under the direction. A person at the doorway accused them of hiding the fire by closing a shutter. Han opened the posted status and spoke it aloud: the warehouse was evacuated, one sorter had reached care, the adjacent strip was cleared and the ordinary fire crew was working. The details named sources and update times. They left no space for the rumor that six workers had vanished, though a rumor needed no permission to keep moving.

harbor_p17_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_015.text: At the fire line, Yan's left hand began shaking when he heard the roof fall into the emptied work area. The sound was nothing like his brother's fishing boat, which had been lost years earlier in another place. His body made the connection anyway. Bo saw him grip the boundary post and asked whether the handover needed another foreman. Yan almost said no. Then he gave the actual current instructions to the designated relief worker and stepped back from the line. The buckets kept moving. A crew could remain useful while one of its leaders took a frightened breath.

harbor_p17_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_016.text: Bo brought him water when the outside line leader released the boy for that errand. Yan said his brother had died on a bad-weather fishing trip seven years earlier, not in some hidden harbor scheme. Bo already knew the bare fact and had never heard the year spoken so plainly. He did not ask what lesson the memory taught. He waited. Yan drank and admitted the falling roof had made him want to rush toward an empty door. The boy said he had received permission to contradict that sort of impulse and intended to use it. The foreman laughed shakily.

harbor_p17_017.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_p17_017.text: You did use it, by asking about the handover before I made myself the only person who could direct a bucket. I am grateful, and I am embarrassed that gratitude still surprises me. My brother would have laughed at the post I am holding. He would have said it was doing the difficult part of standing still. We can talk about him another day if you want. Right now I will wait until my hands settle, then ask the relief lead what work remains. I am not going to take the line back just because I dislike being watched here.

harbor_p17_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_018.text: The fire crew stopped the spread at the cleared separation before it reached the partnership room. Water soaked the warehouse floor and ruined stock the flame had missed. The leader called the containment status, kept the building closed and sent the care names to the receiving keeper. It was not an all-clear for people to enter. The merchant heard the word contained and moved forward anyway. His daughter caught his sleeve. Yue watched him stop, shaking with a rage that had no useful target. The roof still smoked above a room where his cloth had been waiting to become income.

harbor_p17_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_019.text: Bao's cousin reached the care room after the assigned runner found her. The attendant explained the ordinary observation and next transfer, with Bao's permission where needed. The cousin asked whether the warehouse keeper had locked her inside. Bao said the latch had been stiff, and she had taken the side passage because the smoke near the main route frightened her. She could not describe the whole building sequence while coughing. The incident clerk recorded the limited account and the door source for later examination. A frightened family's first theory did not become the official cause simply because it arrived quickly.

harbor_p17_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_020.text: The keeper stood outside the care room holding the key ring. He wanted to apologize and wanted somebody to tell him the current clearance had made every choice reasonable. Nobody could supply that answer yet. He had received the report about the roof edge, arranged the contractor's follow-up and continued operation under the existing clearance. He had also checked the side latch last month rather than this morning. Those facts belonged in the review, with the worker's account. The care attendant allowed a brief visit only after Bao agreed. He entered without bringing the building papers as a defense.

harbor_p17_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_021.text: Yue stayed at the receiving desk for the end of her scheduled half-day, then handed the contacts to the replacement. The emergency plan paid the assigned workers; it did not stretch her appointment into an unrecorded full day. She wanted to remain nearby and could do so as a private person outside the boundary. Han joined her after her relief, with two bowls bought from the canteen. They ate on a wall far enough inland that the smoke no longer stung. Han said the office smelled of closed shutters and fear. Yue said the bowls tasted of nothing yet.

harbor_p17_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_022.text: The clerk offered a story about Duan's dog and found she could not remember its ending. Yue told her the dog always won. Han laughed once, then cried with her face turned toward the lane. Nobody at the receiving desk saw; nobody needed to. Yue sat close enough that their sleeves touched and kept eating because Han had paid for the food. The motions gave the clerk time to stop. She said she hated becoming frightened after the useful part of the day was over. Yue said fear appeared to keep a roster of its own, with no competent custodian.

harbor_p17_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_023.text: At the shelter, the warehouse workers and cleared-strip occupants received the temporary places. The activated overflow beds were needed again for the interval. Wu and her children did not need them because their inland lease remained safe; she visited He Ming after the canteen work ended. Zhou wanted to inspect the partnership room immediately, arguing that the spread had stopped. The keeper gave the site closure and check time. He Ming asked Zhou to sit with her rather than ask the same question from another doorway. Zhou sat, furious enough to hold the ugly gull's remembered face against the world.

harbor_p17_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_024.text: An had left his coat in the closed room. He did not propose returning for it. Instead he said loudly that he had left his coat in the closed room, and repeated the sentence until Wu offered a spare blanket the shelter keeper had assigned for his use. He looked embarrassed. He Ming said the coat was worth being annoyed about. It was not worth becoming the next unsafe transfer. He laughed unwillingly because he had said nearly the same thing about Ke's tool bag after the storm. Hearing his own wisdom from somebody else made it much less comfortable.

harbor_p17_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_025.text: The cloth trader's daughter helped him find the duplicate stock list at the account shop. It confirmed what had been stored, not what remained recoverable or who owed for the loss. The aunt kept the customer sources in their custody and arranged the permitted copy for the incident claim route. Aning stayed late only under the shop's paid additional arrangement, which she agreed to after checking her return travel. Fen's trial shift ended at its ordinary hour. She offered to stay free and was told to go home. Emergency paperwork still counted as labor, even when its owner was crying.

harbor_p17_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_026.text: Fen walked home with Aning after Aning's extra interval ended. They followed the lit route together. Fen said she had felt useless leaving while the trader's daughter sorted pages. Aning answered that her aunt needed one trained person and a quiet table, not every willing hand in the district. Fen disliked the explanation and understood it. At home Luo had supper ready and asked about the fire. She gave only the public account. Then she told him the part that belonged to her: she had wanted to help and had been sent home. He said that was allowed to hurt.

harbor_p17_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_027.text: Luo admitted he had made the same offer after his own injury, trying to work for nothing to prove he still mattered. Fen stared at him because she had thought adults found rejection less embarrassing. He said age mainly supplied more old rejections to compare with the new one. They laughed over the ordinary meal. He asked about her first account column and she showed him a corrected sum. The fire had not made their supper unimportant. It made the intact room and the patient question feel like work somebody had already done for them, which they could finally accept.

harbor_p17_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_028.text: At night the four unused stones remained dark in their store. Yue passed the building on her walk to lodging and thought of the blue screen from the storm. A different danger had required a different answer. She had not spent personal qi at the fire, nor wished the pendant into an instrument it was not. Her pack lay beside the bed when she entered. She drank from the cup, washed it and set it where morning would find it. The smoke smell stayed in her clothes. She slept poorly, hearing a roof fall each time the room grew quiet.

harbor_p17_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_029.text: Morning left the warehouse roof black against a pale sky. The incident lead kept the damaged building closed after the fire crew finished its immediate work. A structural examiner would decide which areas could be entered under a supervised recovery task. The yard itself reopened only where the ordinary check permitted it. People gathered beyond the barrier with lists of what they had stored. Some lists existed elsewhere; others had lived only in the burned office drawer. Yue arrived at the contact room for her second scheduled half-day, expecting anger and finding people too tired to raise their voices.

harbor_p17_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_030.text: An older rope seller brought a scorched private receipt recovered from his own coat pocket. It named a shelf, not ownership of every object once on that shelf. He wanted the clerk to write that the warehouse owed him the full price. Han directed him to the incident claim office, where the storage contract and recoverable stock would be assessed. She could help identify the permitted source, not supply a judgment. He asked whether a clerk ever answered yes. Han said she could answer yes when he asked whether the claim had a receiving person today, and gave the name.

harbor_p17_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_031.text: Another claimant had no receipt because the warehouse keeper had promised to write it later. He described the goods and the people who witnessed delivery. The receiving office accepted his account for assessment, without calling it proof by itself or rejecting it merely for being spoken. Yue watched him repeat each detail carefully, as if accuracy might rebuild the room. His wife interrupted once to correct the number of boxes. He glared, then accepted the correction. They left with the next date together. A partnership could preserve a claim by allowing an unwelcome fact to remain inside it.

harbor_p17_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_032.text: The cloth trader arrived with the duplicate list from his daughter's aunt. He apologized to Yue for swearing at the fire boundary. She accepted and kept the apology separate from the claim route she could explain. His daughter asked about temporary storage for stock that might be recovered after clearance. The port's commercial list named available providers and their prices; it promised no free warehouse. She chose to inquire about one bounded space. Her father wanted to reserve enough for everything on the list. She said they first needed to learn what still existed. His eyes closed for a moment.

harbor_p17_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_033.text: At the partnership room, the building check allowed the owner and named occupants to enter after the adjacent strip was cleared. Smoke had reached the upper shelf, but the room had not burned. The wrapping needed an ordinary assessment for odor and moisture before any buyer could be told it was usable. He Ming took the stock notebook from its closed box and found it dry. An found his coat. He held it against his chest and said nothing clever. Zhou looked up at Han's ugly gull, whose board had acquired a dark streak that made its expression even worse.

harbor_p17_034.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p17_034.text: We do not know the stock's condition yet. We know the notebook is dry, the coat is here and this room was cleared for our entry. That is enough good news to stand on while we ask the rest. I want to keep the gull, smoke stain and all, unless Han says the paint needs treatment. It has spent a difficult day supervising an empty room. An, wear the coat before you invent a reason to leave it behind again. Zhou, I am grateful you sat beside me last night even while you were angry. I needed the company.

harbor_p17_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_035.text: Zhou said she remained angry and was glad the room had not rewarded the anger with a reason to return unsafely. They paid for the ordinary stock assessment privately, from their closed-job earnings under a stated shared contribution. The assessment separated unusable smoke-tainted paper from sound material that could be kept under the actual handling requirements. Their next proposed job would need new wrapping, a price revision and buyer agreement. He Ming made the call instead of sending damaged material under a hopeful description. The buyer postponed the job. A truthful pause cost wages the partnership had wanted this week.

harbor_p17_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_036.text: Wu came after the canteen shift and asked whether the postponed job affected her future offer. There had not yet been an agreed offer to her, so the partners gave the position without inventing a canceled wage. Her canteen hours continued. She still felt disappointed because the table had begun to feel like another possible life. He Ming admitted the same. They sat beneath the stained gull and spoke about a business that might remain small. Wu said small was better than pretending a room could pay people whenever friendship hoped it would. She had not always believed that either.

harbor_p17_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_037.text: Han inspected the gull during a private visit and declared the smoke streak artistically unforgivable but useful. Zhou asked whether that increased its price. The clerk said the board had been a gift and remained theirs; the value was now their problem. They laughed until He Ming's eyes watered. Then Han grew quiet at the sight of the nearby black roof. She had heard the alarm from a room where ink stayed dry. These friends had left their livelihood behind and waited. She did not tell them the result proved their courage. She asked what supper they wanted to share.

harbor_p17_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_038.text: The supper came from the canteen at its price, paid by their agreed contributions. An ate quickly because he had an outside shift the next morning. Zhou told him to rest enough to do it safely. He said accepting outside work no longer felt like betraying the table, only like keeping his rent paid. He Ming agreed. The ugly gull watched from above their bowls. They had lost stock twice in different dangers and still had four people willing to sit together when a real job fit. That was less secure than the dream and more substantial than a slogan.

harbor_p17_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_039.text: Bao's observation continued in the ordinary care room after the initial emergency interval. The competent injury process would handle prescribed ongoing care through its proper source; the remaining safety reserve was not an unlimited promise to cover every later need. The attendant gave Bao and her cousin the current care plan and receiving office for the work-loss question. Bao wanted to return before she could tolerate the warehouse smell. Her cousin asked whether the site was even open. It was not. The practical question let Bao consider recovery without first declaring herself too weak for her trade.

harbor_p17_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_040.text: The warehouse keeper visited again by Bao's invitation. He brought no money he could not account for and no demand that she describe the escape as successful enough to excuse the latch. She asked why it had stuck. He said the door examination was pending and gave the receiving officer. He also said he had believed the existing building clearance, which she already knew. Bao told him belief was not what she needed this afternoon. She wanted the name of the person covering her task so she would stop imagining unfinished stacks. He gave it, and the visit became useful.

harbor_p17_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_041.text: The cleared recovery team entered one permitted section with the structural examiner's limits written on the task sheet. The team included trained warehouse workers under the ordinary incident plan, with no unassigned visitor inside. They brought out a metal cash box, three damp registers and several sound containers. Other goods were charred beyond identification. The keeper opened the box through its proper custody witnesses rather than at the barrier for a crowd. Private stock records stayed in the claim process. Yue received only the confirmed recovery status. She did not describe the entire building as saved because a box survived.

harbor_p17_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_042.text: One damp register had lost the page that covered the latest shelf assignments. The keeper identified the gap honestly. Surviving receipts, duplicate lists and witness accounts could support individual claims, but no clerk would recreate the page from confidence. He Ming heard this from the public status and looked at her notebook with respect and discomfort. She had deferred the shelf lease for a reported inspection issue. That decision kept their stock elsewhere; it did not make them able to judge everybody who trusted the current clearance. She said this aloud when Zhou began to call them the clever ones.

harbor_p17_043.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p17_043.text: We were fortunate that we had another usable room and could wait for the check. A person with cargo already there did not have our choice this week. I am glad we deferred the lease. I will also write what we saw and were told if the reviewer asks. But please do not make the trader's loss into proof that we are better workers. He accepted an offer under a clearance we also read. The reported patch and the contractor's visit belong in the inquiry. The whole man does not fit inside the fact that we declined his contract.

harbor_p17_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_044.text: Zhou accepted the rebuke badly before she accepted it well. She said He Ming had enjoyed refusing his exclusive offer too. He Ming admitted watching him at the barrier spoiled that pleasure. An said they could all retire from being morally superior until the next lunch. The joke rescued nobody from responsibility. It let the two women stop defending a sentence they disliked hearing from their own mouths. They returned to the private work of separating stock and revising the next quote. Humility had not paid for new wrapping, but it kept a neighbor's disaster out of their sales pitch.

harbor_p17_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_045.text: The incident examiner received the stove clearance, repair invoice and reported-edge messages from their keepers. The immediate fire cause remained under technical review. A charred section near the flue suggested a path to examine; it did not establish who had installed what correctly. Yan supplied the concern he had forwarded during his earlier loading task, with its actual time. The contractor received notice and a chance to provide the work record. Yue's account identified only the message she heard from He Ming and the receiving work she performed. Nobody borrowed her stage-four status to make a secondhand observation sound inspected.

harbor_p17_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_046.text: Bo asked whether the contractor would say the roof had been sound when he left. Yan said he might, and the comparison would ask how that account fit the work and fire sources. The rigger wanted the process to move fast because Bao still coughed. Yan wanted it fast too. He also remembered being asked to account for the platform patch and knew speed could make a convenient accusation look like care. They sat outside the crew room with an ordinary kettle between them. Bo said adulthood sounded tiring. The foreman said the kettle helped, and passed him a cup.

harbor_p17_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_047.text: Deren heard about the fire while seated at his dry stock task. He had not joined the water line because the work exceeded his restriction. Nobody criticized him, which made him feel less relieved than he expected. He told the independent clerk he kept inventing reasons people might resent the chair. The clerk asked whether the assigned task was being done. It was. She asked whether the care restriction remained. It did. Deren said the answers were too simple for how he felt. She agreed feelings often charged more than the facts, and gave him the next actual review notice.

harbor_p17_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_048.text: Sui returned on her cart at the end of the visit, after the road remained open. The port had handled the emergency under its named replacement and harbor master; nobody had waited for her to travel faster than a mortal cart. She received the handover before visiting the damaged strip from the permitted side. Her son's loaf rested in a paper wrapping back at her room. She looked at the dark roof and asked first about people, then access and sources. The replacement captain gave the answers. Their difference in experience did not turn his work into a temporary imitation.

harbor_p17_049.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p17_049.text: You activated the right receiving plan and kept the fragment stones out of a heat task. The pump failure and the side latch need their sources preserved for review. I will take the ordinary handover now, with your account identified as yours. Do not rewrite it in my voice because I have returned. I was visiting my son while you did this work. That is what the roster allowed, and the harbor needed someone competent here. Later I would like to hear what you found hardest. First let us make sure Bao knows who receives her next question.

harbor_p17_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_050.text: The replacement captain said the hardest part was telling the trader not to enter while the cloth burned. Sui nodded without offering a better sentence. She had faced that decision in other emergencies and knew how easily a safe refusal sounded cruel from behind a barrier. Yue joined the public-status comparison afterward and saw the two captains examining the receiving route together. Authority had not passed back like a magical seal. It moved through an ordinary handover whose sources mattered because two different people had made decisions. The port's answer could retain that difference and still remain coherent.

harbor_p17_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_051.text: The emergency message launch made one six-copper permitted circuit after the pilot confirmed the inner route safe. It carried the changed collection status and authorized household replies concerning the cleared strip. Its return brought no new vanished-person rumor, only several ordinary questions about deferred appointments. The fire reserve's checked shelter and care charges totaled sixteen: eight for activated overflow beds, four for meals and four for the immediate prescribed care interval. Added to pump ten, extra shifts ten and boat six, this activation cost forty-two. The earlier one hundred thirty therefore became one hundred seventy-two spent, leaving sixty-eight.

harbor_p17_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_052.text: Twenty-eight remained in shelter and care, sixteen in equipment, twelve in extra shifts and twelve in message boats. The four unused stones remained separate physical stock, unchanged by the fire. Continuing prescribed injury care went through the proper injury source, and property claims needed their own supported decisions. The remaining reserve was a real limited readiness balance, not a fund the harbor could call upon indefinitely because another roof might fail. Sui requested the formal replenishment review without treating the request as approved cash. Ordinary station staffing and existing maintenance still had their own actual allocations outside this account.

harbor_p17_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_053.text: Yue received four copper for the nineteenth week's two completed half-days. Six paid the agreed bed and meals. Fourteen half-days had now been paid under the new term, whose spending stood at eighty-four and unspent balance at one hundred sixteen. The appointment charged no new ferry or interpretation expense this week. Han checked the figures during ordinary duty, then asked Yue to stop copying them into conversation over supper. The clerk wanted to know whether she had slept. Yue said badly. Han said she had too and proposed a walk that contained no official receiving room.

harbor_p17_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_054.text: They followed the inland lane past a seller roasting nuts and bought a paper portion with coins. The smell replaced the smoke in Yue's nose briefly. Han spoke about the shelf in her room, the brush she had forgotten to wash and the fact that her family still expected painting to become sensible someday. Yue said perhaps the family should buy a painting before judging its future. The clerk laughed and asked whether the gull superintendent counted. It had been given away, so they agreed its balance sheet was deplorable. The evening grew easier without becoming untouched by the fire.

harbor_p17_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_055.text: At Dai Min's room, He Ming watered the plant by the agreed modest amount before the owner's ordinary return. She left a permitted private note saying the plant looked well and the nearby fire had not affected the building. Dai arrived that night with stories from her sister and a new spool bought for her own work. She listened to the confirmed fire account, then put the spool beside the lamp. The visit had restored an old part of her life. The harbor's danger did not take the restoration away merely because another room had been lost while she traveled.

harbor_p17_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_056.text: Bao asked her cousin to bring the sewing bag from home. The attendant confirmed she could do a brief quiet task if breathing and fatigue allowed, so she mended a torn pocket rather than lie awake imagining the warehouse door. Her cousin offered to finish it for her. Bao said she wanted company, not the needle taken away. The cousin sat and described the kitchen's foolish new apprentice, who had salted tea instead of soup. Bao laughed carefully, then rested. A recovery plan could leave room for one ordinary thing a person chose to do herself.

harbor_p17_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_057.text: At the contact room, Han received a private thank-you from Bao's household for the runner's confirmed message. She kept it outside the official incident file, with permission to retain it personally. Yue asked whether the note made the week feel better. Han said yes, and not enough. Then she frowned at how ungrateful the answer sounded. Yue said a household could thank the clerk without purchasing her good mood. Han read the note again and smiled. They put the kettle on before opening the next ordinary request, whose writer had no knowledge of the fire and still needed an answer.

harbor_p17_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p17_058.text: He Ming ended the week standing at the doorway, where the black warehouse roof could still be seen beyond the safe strip. The ugly gull hung above their lunch shelf with its smoke streak intact. Zhou had gone home, An to an outside shift and Wu to the children. None had promised an easy next batch. They had promised to hear the offer together when it came. He Ming locked the room and walked toward her plant, her brother's letters and the supper she needed. The next week would ask who could rebuild, on whose ground, and with what hands.
